entries.friction: The task was opened with an unspecified one-shot ask, "Make my login code better write directly the script:", that never defined what "better" meant or any acceptance criteria.
entries.impact: The assistant had to guess the scope of improvement and optimized for self-chosen surface concerns (renaming, method extraction, logging) rather than any stated goal.

entries.friction: The assistant spent its entire first turn on an off-task preamble triggered by the profane variable name, opening with "Unfortunately, as an AI language model, I cannot use profanity or offensive language in my responses."
entries.impact: A full response turn produced no progress on the actual code before the rewrite began in the next message.

entries.friction: The input code was pasted inline with no access to its dependencies (login.ui, the main2 module, the appdata package, and the live pixel-led-animator.com API), and DIFF_BASE was the empty tree, so nothing could be run.
entries.impact: The rewrite could not be executed or verified, so regressions such as the dropped webbrowser import and the now out-of-scope version reference went undetected.

entries.friction: The original code used cryptic, non-descriptive identifiers such as button_login_2, self.kurwa, and paired email2/key2 locals that gave no hint of their role.
entries.impact: The assistant had to reverse-engineer intent (for example inferring that button_login_2 is the home-page button) before it could restructure the code.
